name: What is considered a multifamily property in Miami-Dade County?

mainEntity.name: What is considered a multifamily property in Miami-Dade County?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Miami-Dade County and other South Florida areas, a multifamily property typically refers to residential buildings with two or more dwelling units, such as duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, or larger apartment complexes. These properties are primarily used for rental income and are attractive to investors seeking consistent cash flow and potential appreciation. Understanding the local zoning and property classifications is crucial, as regulations can vary significantly even within nearby cities like Miami, Coral Gables, or Miami Beach, influencing what types of multifamily units can be built or modified.
acceptedAnswer.description: Multifamily properties in Miami-Dade County are residential buildings with two or more dwelling units, like duplexes or apartment complexes, primarily for rental income. Local zoning regulations determine specific classifications and allowable uses.
